entries.name: HVAC controls
entries.definition: The sensors, thermostats and controllers that regulate heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment.

entries.name: Hybrid mobile app development
entries.definition: Building mobile apps with web technologies such as HTML, CSS and JavaScript inside a native container, so one code base runs on several platforms.

entries.name: Hydraulic snubbing
entries.definition: An oil-well service technique in which a hydraulic unit pushes pipe into, or pulls it out of, a well that is under pressure.

entries.name: Hydrological modelling
entries.definition: Using mathematical models to simulate how water moves through catchments, rivers and aquifers.

entries.name: Hyperbaric welding
entries.definition: Welding carried out at raised pressure, usually inside a sealed dry chamber around underwater structures such as pipelines.

entries.name: Hypercompact stellar systems
entries.definition: Dense clusters of stars predicted to stay bound to a supermassive black hole that has been flung out of its host galaxy.

entries.name: I2C
entries.definition: A two-wire serial bus protocol, created by Philips, that lets chips on a circuit board talk to each other.

entries.name: iAd
entries.definition: Apple's mobile advertising platform, which served ads inside iOS apps until it was shut down in 2016.

entries.name: IAR Embedded Workbench
entries.definition: An integrated development environment from IAR Systems, with a C and C++ compiler and debugger, for writing embedded software for microcontrollers.

entries.name: iBeacon
entries.definition: Apple's Bluetooth Low Energy technology in which a small transmitter broadcasts an identifier that nearby phones can detect, used for indoor location and proximity.

entries.name: IBM Bluemix
entries.definition: IBM's cloud platform for building and running applications, renamed IBM Cloud in 2017.

entries.name: IBM Business Process Manager
entries.definition: IBM software for modelling, running and monitoring business processes, later succeeded by IBM Business Automation Workflow.

entries.name: IBM CL/SuperSession
entries.definition: Mainframe software that manages a terminal user's sessions with several network applications at once.

entries.name: IBM Data Studio
entries.definition: An Eclipse-based IBM tool for administering and developing Db2 databases.

entries.name: IBM eServer
entries.definition: IBM's server brand of the early 2000s, covering the xSeries, pSeries, iSeries and zSeries hardware lines.

entries.name: IBM FileNet
entries.definition: IBM's enterprise content management and business process platform for storing, managing and routing documents.

entries.name: IBM Informix
entries.definition: A relational database management system that IBM bought in 2001 and that is now developed and sold by HCL.

entries.name: IBM OfficeVision
entries.definition: IBM's office software for mainframes, offering email, calendars and document handling.

entries.name: IBM POWER10
entries.definition: IBM's tenth-generation POWER microprocessor family for servers, released in 2021.

entries.name: IBM POWER7
entries.definition: IBM's seventh-generation POWER microprocessor family for servers, released in 2010.

entries.name: IBM POWER8
entries.definition: IBM's eighth-generation POWER microprocessor family for servers, released in 2014.

entries.name: IBM POWER9
entries.definition: IBM's ninth-generation POWER microprocessor family for servers, released in 2017.

entries.name: IBM QRadar
entries.definition: Security information and event management (SIEM) software that collects and analyses log and network data to detect threats.

entries.name: IBM Rational Application Developer
entries.definition: An Eclipse-based IBM development environment for building Java and web applications, aimed at deployment on IBM WebSphere.

entries.name: IBM Tivoli Enterprise Console
entries.definition: An IBM event-management product that collects events from monitored systems and applications, correlates them and triggers automated responses.

entries.name: IBM WebSphere Application Server
entries.definition: IBM's Java application server, which runs and manages enterprise web applications.

entries.name: ICD coding
entries.definition: Assigning International Classification of Diseases codes to diagnoses and procedures in medical records for billing and statistics.

entries.name: ICH guidelines
entries.definition: Technical guidelines from the International Council for Harmonisation that set common expectations for the quality, safety and efficacy of medicines and for how clinical trials are run.

entries.name: ICMPv6
entries.definition: The Internet Control Message Protocol for IPv6, used for error messages, diagnostics and neighbour discovery.

entries.name: IDA Pro
entries.definition: An interactive disassembler and debugger from Hex-Rays for reverse engineering compiled programs.

entries.name: Ideation
entries.definition: Coming up with and developing new ideas, for example for products, designs or campaigns.

entries.name: Identity management
entries.definition: Creating, maintaining and removing the digital identities of people and systems and controlling what access those identities have.

entries.name: IDS InfoLease
entries.definition: Software for managing leases and other asset-finance contracts.

entries.name: IEEE 1394
entries.definition: An IEEE standard for a high-speed serial bus connecting devices such as cameras and disk drives, sold by Apple as FireWire.

entries.name: IEEE 1547
entries.definition: An IEEE standard setting technical requirements for connecting distributed energy resources, such as solar inverters and batteries, to the electric power grid.

entries.name: IFS Applications
entries.definition: Enterprise resource planning software from the Swedish company IFS, whose current product line is branded IFS Cloud.

entries.name: IIS Manager
entries.definition: The graphical console in Windows for configuring Microsoft Internet Information Services web sites and application pools.

entries.name: iMac G4
entries.definition: Apple's all-in-one desktop computer with a flat display on an adjustable arm, sold from 2002 to 2004.

entries.name: iMac G5
entries.definition: Apple's all-in-one desktop computer with a PowerPC G5 processor, sold from 2004 to 2006.

entries.name: Image and video compression
entries.definition: Reducing the storage and bandwidth that pictures and video need by encoding them with formats and codecs such as JPEG and H.264.
